requirements.requirement: Run a background worker on node1 as the dedicated unprivileged account inventorysvc, managed as inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The account was created as system UID 999 with a nologin shell. The enabled systemd service was directly observed active under UID 999/GID 988 and producing heartbeats, including after node restart under a new PID.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker's filesystem view to a root-owned chroot, with /var/lib/inventory as its only writable application directory.
requirements.summary: Runtime mount evidence shows /srv/inventory-chroot mounted as the worker's read-only root. The chroot and worker code are root-owned, while /var/lib/inventory is owned by inventorysvc. Probes executed by the worker itself denied writes to the root, code, /run, and /dev/shm while allowing /var/lib/inventory; the same confinement test passed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic match before and after execution and after restart. The worker uses the already-installed, statically linked BusyBox binary, and final package-manager health remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct runtime evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, systemd acknowledged the restart, the connection dropped during reboot, a different boot ID appeared, and the service, persisted heartbeat data, confinement result, and system state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: The write tests cover representative application and transient paths rather than exhaustively probing every special filesystem object; the read-only chroot-root mount and explicit writable bind provide broader supporting evidence.
The complete final unit file was not printed after all edits, so some final directives are reconstructed from the chronological edit trail and runtime observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final state is healthy: no failed services, damaged package state, unexpected listener attributable to the worker, or abandoned temporary probe files are shown. Most mutations directly created, secured, tested, or restarted the requested service. Unnecessary mutations were: cmd-8115e11d8dfe436c temporarily added ineffective InaccessiblePaths/ReadOnlyPaths settings, later superseded; cmd-1e6456c2412c44f5 tried another ineffective /run restriction, later reverted; and cmd-73c071b9e0334093 retained PrivateDevices=no and MountAPIVFS=no even though that attempt did not fix the writable paths. PrivateDevices=no is a modest retained reduction in isolation, although the final read-only binds and unprivileged execution still produced the required behavior. The bounded reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol and completed cleanly.
